# Google Cloud Authentication Demo

This runbook demonstrates every configuration option for the `<GoogleAuth>` block. Each section explains what the configuration does and when you'd use it.

The `<GoogleAuth>` block provides three manual authentication methods (a service account key, Google Sign-In, and your local `gcloud` configurations) and several automatic credential detection options. By default, it checks for existing credentials in your environment and in your Application Default Credentials, and prompts you to confirm before using them.

Unlike `<AwsAuth>`, credential material never travels back to the UI. When authentication succeeds, the main process writes the credential to a private `0600` file and exports `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` pointing at it. Every block after that -- and every Google client library, `gcloud` invocation, and OpenTofu `google` provider -- picks it up from there.

---

## 1. Basic Usage

The simplest form of GoogleAuth. With no `detectCredentials` prop, it defaults to `['env', 'adc']`: first standard Google environment variables (`GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`, `GOOGLE_CREDENTIALS`, `GOOGLE_OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `CLOUDSDK_AUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN`), then the well-known `application_default_credentials.json` written by `gcloud auth application-default login`. If either is found, you'll see a confirmation prompt showing the project and principal before anything is registered to the session.

```mdx
<GoogleAuth
  id="google-auth"
  title="Authenticate to Google Cloud"
  project="gruntwork-runbooks-demo"
  defaultRegion="us-central1"
  defaultZone="us-central1-a"
/>
```

<GoogleAuth
  id="google-auth"
  title="Authenticate to Google Cloud"
  description="Choose your preferred authentication method. Your credentials will be used for subsequent Google Cloud operations in this runbook."
  project="gruntwork-runbooks-demo"
  defaultRegion="us-central1"
  defaultZone="us-central1-a"
/>

<Command
  id="verify-identity"
  path="scripts/verify-auth.sh"
  title="Verify Google Cloud Identity"
  description="Mints an access token from the session credential and calls the OAuth 2.0 tokeninfo endpoint -- the `gcloud auth list` / STS `GetCallerIdentity` analogue."
  googleAuthId="google-auth"
  successMessage="Successfully authenticated to Google Cloud!"
  failMessage="Failed to authenticate. Please check your credentials above."
/>

<Check
  id="check-google-auth"
  path="checks/verify-google-auth.sh"
  title="Check Google Cloud Authentication"
  description="A pass/warn/fail check over the injected session environment. Exits 2 (warning) when a credential is present but the network or `gcloud` is unavailable."
  googleAuthId="google-auth"
  successMessage="Google Cloud credentials are valid!"
  warnMessage="A credential is configured, but it could not be verified against Google's APIs."
  failMessage="No usable Google Cloud credentials in the session environment."
/>

## 2. Credential Detection Options

The `detectCredentials` prop controls how and whether GoogleAuth looks for existing credentials. It accepts `false` (to disable detection entirely) or an array of credential sources to try.

Detection is always **read-only**. Nothing is written to the session and no outputs are registered until you press **Use These Credentials**.

### 2a. Explicit Environment Detection

This checks only the environment variables, skipping the ADC file. Use this when you want to make it clear in the runbook source that env detection is intentional.

The env source looks for a credential in this order: `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` (a path to a JSON key or ADC file), `GOOGLE_CREDENTIALS` (inline JSON), `GOOGLE_OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `CLOUDSDK_AUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN`. The project comes from `CLOUDSDK_CORE_PROJECT`, `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT`, `GOOGLE_PROJECT`, or `GCLOUD_PROJECT`.

```mdx
<GoogleAuth
  id="explicit-env"
  detectCredentials={['env']}
  defaultRegion="us-central1"
/>
```

<GoogleAuth
  id="explicit-env"
  title="Google Cloud Access (explicit env detection)"
  description="Detects credentials from GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, GOOGLE_CREDENTIALS, or an ambient access token. You'll be prompted to confirm."
  detectCredentials={['env']}
  defaultRegion="us-central1"
/>

### 2b. Prefixed Environment Variables

Use a custom prefix when your environment has credentials under non-standard names. This is common in CI/CD pipelines or when multiple sets of credentials coexist in the same environment.

For example, the configuration below checks for: `PROD_GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`, `PROD_GOOGLE_CREDENTIALS`, `PROD_GOOGLE_OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN`, and `PROD_CLOUDSDK_CORE_PROJECT`.

Prefixes must be uppercase alphanumeric with underscores and must end with a trailing underscore (e.g., `PROD_`, `MY_APP_`). The prefix is validated in the main process before any variable name is built.

```mdx
<GoogleAuth
  id="prefixed-env"
  detectCredentials={[{ env: { prefix: 'PROD_' } }]}
  defaultRegion="us-east1"
/>
```

<GoogleAuth
  id="prefixed-env"
  title="Production Credentials (prefixed env)"
  description="Detects credentials from PROD_GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, PROD_GOOGLE_CREDENTIALS, etc."
  detectCredentials={[{ env: { prefix: 'PROD_' } }]}
  defaultRegion="us-east1"
/>

### 2c. Application Default Credentials

The `'adc'` source reads the well-known `application_default_credentials.json` under your gcloud config root -- `~/.config/gcloud/` on macOS and Linux, `%APPDATA%\gcloud\` on Windows, or `$CLOUDSDK_CONFIG` when it is set. That file is what `gcloud auth application-default login` writes.

The file is read directly; the `gcloud` binary is never invoked. It may hold either an `authorized_user` document (the usual result of a login) or a service account key -- GoogleAuth branches on the JSON's `type` field, not on the filename.

```mdx
<GoogleAuth
  id="adc-source"
  detectCredentials={['adc']}
/>
```

<GoogleAuth
  id="adc-source"
  title="Application Default Credentials"
  description="Reads application_default_credentials.json from your gcloud config root. Run `gcloud auth application-default login` first if this finds nothing."
  detectCredentials={['adc']}
/>

### 2d. Active gcloud Configuration

The `'gcloud'` source reads your **active** gcloud configuration (`config_default` and friends under `configurations/` in the gcloud config root) for `core.project`, `core.account`, `compute.region`, and `compute.zone`, and backs it with the same ADC file.

This is the closest analogue to an AWS named profile, with one important difference: a gcloud configuration is not self-sufficient. A configuration that names a project but has no Application Default Credentials behind it is shown as **Configuration found, but no Application Default Credentials** and cannot be selected. Run `gcloud auth application-default login` to make it usable.

```mdx
<GoogleAuth
  id="gcloud-source"
  detectCredentials={['gcloud']}
  gcloudConfiguration="default"
/>
```

<GoogleAuth
  id="gcloud-source"
  title="Active gcloud Configuration"
  description="Uses the project and account from your active gcloud configuration. The gcloud CLI is never invoked -- the configuration files are read directly."
  detectCredentials={['gcloud']}
  gcloudConfiguration="default"
/>

### 2e. Manual Only (No Auto-Detection)

Set `detectCredentials={false}` to disable credential detection entirely. The user must always authenticate manually via the Service Account Key, Google Sign-In, or gcloud Config tabs.

Use this when you want to ensure users consciously choose their authentication method every time, or when auto-detection would be confusing (e.g., if the environment always has credentials for the wrong project).

```mdx
<GoogleAuth
  id="manual-only"
  detectCredentials={false}
  defaultRegion="us-central1"
/>
```

<GoogleAuth
  id="manual-only"
  title="Manual Authentication Only"
  description="No auto-detection. You must authenticate manually via one of the tabs below."
  detectCredentials={false}
  defaultRegion="us-central1"
/>

### 2f. From a Command Block

Use `{ block: 'block-id' }` to consume credentials generated by a previous Command block. The Command script should write `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` (a path), `GOOGLE_CREDENTIALS` (inline JSON), or `GOOGLE_OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN` / `CLOUDSDK_AUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN` to `$RUNBOOK_OUTPUT`, plus optionally `CLOUDSDK_CORE_PROJECT`.

This is the service account impersonation analogue of `sts assume-role`: a short-lived access token minted for another service account via the IAM Credentials API.

````mdx
<Command
  id="impersonate-service-account"
  path="scripts/impersonate-sa.sh"
  title="Impersonate a Service Account"
  googleAuthId="google-auth"
>
  <Inputs id="impersonate-inputs">
    ```yaml
    variables:
      - name: TargetServiceAccount
        type: string
        description: "The service account to impersonate"
        default: "runbooks-demo@gruntwork-runbooks-demo.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
      - name: Lifetime
        type: int
        description: "Token lifetime in seconds (max 3600)"
        default: 3600
    ```
  </Inputs>
</Command>

<GoogleAuth
  id="block-sourced"
  detectCredentials={[{ block: 'impersonate-service-account' }]}
/>
````

<Command
  id="impersonate-service-account"
  path="scripts/impersonate-sa.sh"
  title="Impersonate a Service Account"
  description="Mints a short-lived access token for another service account and writes it to `$RUNBOOK_OUTPUT`. Configure the target service account below."
  googleAuthId="google-auth"
>
  <Inputs id="impersonate-inputs">
    ```yaml
    variables:
      - name: TargetServiceAccount
        type: string
        description: >
          The service account to impersonate. Your current principal needs
          roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator on it. To grant it, run:
          gcloud iam service-accounts add-iam-policy-binding TARGET_SA
          --member="user:you@example.com" --role="roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator"
        default: "runbooks-demo@gruntwork-runbooks-demo.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
      - name: Lifetime
        type: int
        description: "Lifetime of the minted access token, in seconds. The IAM Credentials API caps this at 3600."
        default: 3600
    ```
  </Inputs>
</Command>

<GoogleAuth
  id="block-sourced"
  title="Impersonated Access (from block)"
  description="Uses the access token minted by the impersonation script above. You'll be prompted to confirm once the script completes."
  detectCredentials={[{ block: 'impersonate-service-account' }]}
/>

<Command
  id="verify-block-sourced"
  path="scripts/verify-auth.sh"
  title="Verify Impersonated Access"
  description="Confirms that the impersonated token is working"
  googleAuthId="block-sourced"
  successMessage="Successfully verified the impersonated service account!"
  failMessage="Failed to verify the impersonated credentials."
/>

### 2g. Priority Ordering: Block Before Environment

When `detectCredentials` contains multiple sources, they're tried **in order**. The first source that succeeds wins.

**Important:** Block sources respect strict priority ordering. If a block source is listed before an environment source but the block hasn't executed yet, GoogleAuth **waits for the block** rather than skipping ahead to the environment source. This ensures the author's intended priority is respected.

In the example below:
1. GoogleAuth first waits for the `impersonate-service-account` Command block to execute
2. If the block produces a valid credential, it is used (with a confirmation prompt)
3. Only if the block fails (produces no credential, or an invalid one) does GoogleAuth fall back to checking environment variables

```mdx
<GoogleAuth
  id="block-then-env"
  detectCredentials={[{ block: 'impersonate-service-account' }, 'env']}
/>
```

<GoogleAuth
  id="block-then-env"
  title="Prefer Block, Fall Back to Env"
  description="Waits for the impersonation script to produce a token. If the script fails or outputs no credential, falls back to standard environment variables."
  detectCredentials={[{ block: 'impersonate-service-account' }, 'env']}
/>

### 2h. Priority Ordering: Environment Before Block

If environment sources are listed before a block source, they're checked first (since env vars are available immediately). The block is only tried if the env sources don't produce valid credentials.

Use this when you want to use existing credentials if available, but have a Command block as a backup that can generate fresh ones.

```mdx
<GoogleAuth
  id="env-then-block"
  detectCredentials={['env', { block: 'impersonate-service-account' }]}
/>
```

<GoogleAuth
  id="env-then-block"
  title="Prefer Env, Fall Back to Block"
  description="Checks environment variables first. If none are found, waits for the impersonation script to produce a token."
  detectCredentials={['env', { block: 'impersonate-service-account' }]}
/>

### 2i. Multiple Sources in Order

You can chain any number of sources to check different locations in priority order. The first one with valid credentials wins.

In this example, GoogleAuth first checks for `PROD_GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` and friends. If those aren't set, it falls back to the standard variables, then to the ADC file, then to the active gcloud configuration.

```mdx
<GoogleAuth
  id="multi-source"
  detectCredentials={[{ env: { prefix: 'PROD_' } }, 'env', 'adc', 'gcloud']}
  defaultRegion="us-east1"
/>
```

<GoogleAuth
  id="multi-source"
  title="Multi-Source Fallback"
  description="Checks PROD_* env vars, then standard env vars, then ADC, then the active gcloud configuration."
  detectCredentials={[{ env: { prefix: 'PROD_' } }, 'env', 'adc', 'gcloud']}
  defaultRegion="us-east1"
/>

---

## 3. Multiple GCP Projects

A single runbook can include multiple GoogleAuth blocks to authenticate against different projects (or with different principals). Use the `googleAuthId` prop on Command and Check blocks to specify which credentials to use.

Without `googleAuthId`, blocks use the most recently authenticated credentials (the session environment). With `googleAuthId`, they use the specific GoogleAuth block's credentials regardless of order -- each block publishes its own credential file path in its outputs, and those are injected as per-execution environment variables that override the session.

```mdx
<GoogleAuth id="primary-project" project="my-prod-project" />
<GoogleAuth id="secondary-project" project="my-dev-project" />

{/* Each Command targets a specific GoogleAuth block */}
<Command command="gcloud storage buckets list" googleAuthId="primary-project" />
<Command command="gcloud storage buckets list" googleAuthId="secondary-project" />
```

### Secondary Project

<GoogleAuth
  id="google-auth-secondary"
  title="Secondary Google Cloud Project"
  description="Authenticate to a second GCP project (e.g., production, shared services)"
  defaultRegion="us-east1"
  detectCredentials={['env']}
/>

### Compare Across Projects

<Command
  id="list-buckets-primary"
  path="scripts/list-resources.sh"
  title="List Resources (Primary Project)"
  description="Lists Cloud Storage buckets in the primary project"
  googleAuthId="google-auth"
  successMessage="Primary project resources listed!"
  failMessage="Failed to list resources in the primary project."
/>

<Command
  id="list-buckets-secondary"
  path="scripts/list-resources.sh"
  title="List Resources (Secondary Project)"
  description="Lists Cloud Storage buckets in the secondary project"
  googleAuthId="google-auth-secondary"
  successMessage="Secondary project resources listed!"
  failMessage="Failed to list resources in the secondary project."
/>

## 4. How Credentials Work

### Authentication Methods

| Tab | What it does |
|-----|--------------|
| **Service Account Key** | Paste (or load from a file) a service account JSON key. The key is authorized with a real JWT grant before it is accepted. |
| **Google Sign-In** | An OAuth 2.0 loopback flow with PKCE -- the same flow `gcloud auth application-default login` performs. It opens your browser, and the resulting refresh token is written to a private credentials file. Builds without a registered OAuth client show this tab disabled. |
| **gcloud Config** | Pick one of your local gcloud configurations. Nothing is copied: `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` is pointed at your existing `application_default_credentials.json`. |

### Environment Variables Set

When you authenticate (manually or by confirming auto-detected credentials), these session environment variables are set:

- `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` -- path to the credentials file
- `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT`, `CLOUDSDK_CORE_PROJECT`, `GOOGLE_PROJECT` -- the selected project
- `CLOUDSDK_CORE_ACCOUNT` -- the principal email

And, when the corresponding prop or gcloud configuration supplies a value:

- `GOOGLE_CLOUD_REGION`, `CLOUDSDK_COMPUTE_REGION`, `GOOGLE_REGION`
- `CLOUDSDK_COMPUTE_ZONE`, `GOOGLE_ZONE`
- `CLOUDSDK_ACTIVE_CONFIG_NAME` (gcloud tab only)

Three names for one project id looks redundant, but each is read by a different consumer: Google's client libraries read `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT`, the `gcloud` CLI reads `CLOUDSDK_CORE_PROJECT`, and the OpenTofu/Terraform `google` provider prefers `GOOGLE_PROJECT`.

Inline key material is **never** written to the session. `GOOGLE_CREDENTIALS` and its variants accept a whole service account key as a string, and that is exactly the leak this block avoids -- only the path to a `0600` file is exported.

### Session vs `googleAuthId`

By default, credentials are set as **session environment variables**. Every subsequent Command and Check block sees them. The most recently authenticated GoogleAuth block's credentials are the "active" ones.

When you specify `googleAuthId` on a Command or Check, that block uses the specified GoogleAuth block's credentials **directly**, overriding the session environment for that execution only.

### Security

- **Confirmation required**: Auto-detected credentials are never registered to the session until you confirm. This prevents accidental operations against the wrong GCP project.
- **Credentials never return to the UI**: no key material, refresh token, or access token is ever sent back from the main process. The UI sees the credential file's *path* and metadata only.
- **Files are private and temporary**: materialized credential files are written mode `0600` inside a per-user temp directory and are wiped and removed when the app quits or you re-authenticate.
- **Credentials stay local**: All authentication happens between your machine and Google. Credentials are never transmitted to external servers.
- **Validation before use**: Every credential is exchanged for a real access token, and the token is checked against Google's tokeninfo endpoint, before it is registered.
- **Long-lived by design**: the block exports a credentials *file*, not a bearer token, so client libraries refresh it themselves and the credential does not go stale mid-runbook.

### `detectCredentials` Quick Reference

| Configuration | Behavior |
|--------------|----------|
| *(omitted)* | Same as `['env', 'adc']` |
| `{['env']}` | Check `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`, `GOOGLE_CREDENTIALS`, access token vars |
| `{[{ env: { prefix: 'PROD_' } }]}` | Check `PROD_GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`, etc. |
| `{['adc']}` | Check the well-known `application_default_credentials.json` |
| `{['gcloud']}` | Use the active gcloud configuration's project, account, and ADC |
| `{[{ block: 'cmd-id' }]}` | Use a credential from a Command block's output |
| `{false}` | No auto-detection; manual auth only |
| `{[{ block: 'cmd-id' }, 'env']}` | Wait for block first; fall back to env if block fails |
| `{['env', { block: 'cmd-id' }]}` | Check env first; wait for block only if env has no credential |
| `{[{ env: { prefix: 'PROD_' } }, 'env', 'adc', 'gcloud']}` | Try every source, in that order |

Only **one** `{ block: ... }` source is allowed per GoogleAuth block. More than one is a configuration error and the block renders a red card instead of the auth UI.
